description: Generated PDF artifact of the offer terms, distinct from the structured offer record. Versioned in lockstep with offer_versions. Carries template_id, render timestamp, e-sign envelope link.

Reusable letter template with merge tokens (candidate name, role, base salary, start date, equity, bonus terms). Versioned. Renders offer_letter_documents at offer time. Carries template name, body, token schema, jurisdiction, language, active flag, and version.

Versioned snapshot of a job_offer during negotiation (initial -> counter -> revised -> accepted). Each version carries the structured terms (base, bonus, equity, start_date) and the author of the change.

Periodic status update on an okr_objective or key_result during the active cycle. Cadence-of-record (weekly/bi-weekly) for OKR programs. May discuss individual performance — flagged as personal content.
Measurable result attached to an okr_objective. The unit of scoring on OKR programs — vendors universally model KR as first-class (Asana, Monday, ClickUp, Workfront).

Hierarchical objective with measurable key results, weighted progress rollup from child objectives or linked work_items, owner accountability, and cadence (quarterly/annual). Mastered by three distinct domains: WORK-MGMT (team-level execution OKRs), SPM (strategic portfolio OKRs), TALENT-MGMT (individual performance-management OKRs). Same primitive, three different lifecycles and review processes — canonical Signal-1 multi-master.

Group of new hires onboarding together (campus intake class, training boot-camp batch, executive cohort, frontline class). Enables shared activities (group orientation, cohort meetings) and cohort-level analytics distinct from the per-journey view.

Record of paperwork collected from a new hire as part of the journey: I-9, NDA, handbook acknowledgment, direct-deposit form, country-specific tax forms, country-specific work-permit evidence. Captures signature state, external e-signature envelope reference ids, and audit metadata. Distinct from the canonical document templates, which would be mastered by a Document Management domain (not yet in catalog).

Instance of an onboarding plan applied to a specific new hire. Materialized when offer.accepted (ATS) or employee.created (HCM) fires. Carries the bound employee_id, assigned tasks, completion state, current stage, and milestone timestamps (pre-boarding start, Day-1 reached, 30/60/90 completion).

Reusable template defining the stages, tasks, timing, and assignees that make up an onboarding journey for a class of new hire (e.g. engineering, sales, executive, hourly retail, contractor). Plans are versioned and selected based on role / location / employment type when a journey is instantiated.
Phase within a plan or journey (pre-boarding, Day-1, week-1, month-1, 30/60/90 day). Defines task grouping, expected duration, and gate conditions. Stages can be sequenced or run in parallel.

Discrete to-do within a journey: sign I-9, attend orientation, complete compliance training, meet buddy, receive laptop. Carries assignee (new hire / manager / IT / facilities / HR), due date, completion state, evidence, and task type (form / training / meeting / provisioning / acknowledgment). Many tasks are local; a subset triggers cross-domain handoffs into ITSM, IWMS, Payroll, LMS, IGA, or HRSD.

Formal model of concepts (OWL classes / RDF schemas / labeled-property-graph schemas), properties, relationships, hierarchies, and axioms. Includes namespaces, prefixes, imports, and constraint shapes (SHACL/SHEX). The 'schema' tier of a knowledge graph.

QBR, MBR, and WBR operating-cadence meeting records. Carries agenda, participants, structured commentary against initiatives and KRs, action items, and outcome summary. Once closed, the record is locked as the audit trail of the cadence.
CRDs + controller deployments (certificate management, monitoring, GitOps controllers, lifecycle operators).
Employee expression of interest in an internal opportunity, with status workflow (submitted, reviewed, accepted, rejected, withdrawn).
Equity pool reserved for employee grants. Tracks pool size, available headroom, reservation workflows, board-approved expansions.
A reusable multichannel play: triggers, audience, channel sequence, and exit criteria.
Inventory-allocation decision per order line across warehouses/stores/3PLs. State: allocated / partially_allocated / backorder_pending. Core OMS function for split orders and cross-dock routing.
Individual product line within an order: quantity, price, discount, tax breakdown. Parent = orders (cascade delete).

Proposed structure changes: new positions, eliminated positions, reporting-line changes, span-of-control adjustments, layer-level redesign. Carries current vs proposed state and the migration path between them.

Node in the organizational hierarchy: division, business unit, department, team. Carries manager, cost center alignment, geographic scope, and parent/child relationships. HCM masters the operational hierarchy; EPM contributes the cost-center mapping (which would be Finance-mastered once a Finance/GL domain is loaded).
The OSHA Form 300 log of work-related injuries and illnesses, maintained per establishment per year, with the annual 300A summary.
The OSHA Form 301 injury and illness incident report filed per recordable incident.

Unplanned loss-of-service affecting one or more service_connections: detection time, cause (storm / fault / equipment failure / load), estimated restoration, affected customer count. Distinct from ITSM `incidents` (IT) and EAM `eam_work_orders`.

One ordered step within an outreach sequence: the channel, the day offset from enrollment, the message template, and whether the step is automated or requires a recruiter action. Defines the cadence the platform follows when a candidate is enrolled in the parent sequence.

Named multi-step sourcing cadence definition (for example day 0 email, day 3 nudge, day 7 message) that automates candidate outreach. Holds the sequence name, owner, channel mix, and active status, and is the parent of its ordered steps.

Engagement with external law firm/counsel: firm, attorney, matter reference, scope, billing arrangement (hourly / fixed / contingent), budget, contract reference, status. Tracks spend and coordination.
Backing service (database, queue, cache, logging) per app: type, plan, provisioning status, plan cost.
Core app record: name, slug, region, buildpack/runtime, git repo, environment variables, domain bindings.
CI-side artifact capture: buildpack output, slug size, build time, buildpack version, env changes.
Activation/release record: app reference, version/commit, build status, release timestamp, deployment status (success / rollback / in_progress), deployer.
Multi-tenancy: dev/staging/prod with env-specific config overrides, resource limits, addon bindings.
Running compute unit (generic process container): type/size, process type, uptime, memory/CPU metrics, status.
An assignment of a mob to a paddock for a grazing period, with start and end dates, stocking rate, and expected versus actual rest. The junction that realizes a grazing plan on the ground.

A scheduled or ad-hoc deployment of OS or third-party patches to a defined set of endpoints, with per-endpoint approval, execution status, success/failure, and rollback state. Tied to maintenance windows and approval workflows.

Scheduled visit between patient and provider: provider, location, scheduled time, visit type (new / follow-up / annual / urgent), status (scheduled / confirmed / arrived / completed / no-show / canceled), reason for visit. Drives front-of-house workflow and resource utilization.

Provider-initiated request for specialist consultation or external service: referring provider, target specialist/facility, clinical indication, urgency, status (requested / scheduled / completed / declined), insurance authorization status. Drives in-network coordination and revenue capture.

A single payroll cycle execution, scoped to pay group, country, and pay period. Drives gross-to-net calculation across the eligible employee population and produces pay_slips, payroll_journal_entries, and tax_filings. The atomic unit of payroll operations.

Per-employee per-cycle gross-to-net statement: earnings, pre/post-tax deductions, employer contributions, tax withholdings, net pay, YTD totals. Called Pay Stub (US), Payslip (UK/AU/IE), Bulletin de Paie (FR), Lohnzettel (DE), Holerite (BR). Worker-portal accessible; legally retained per jurisdiction.
Scheduled batch of supplier payments grouped by bank_account, currency, payment method (ACH, wire, check, SEPA). Drives the AP payment cycle.
Payment attempt / authorization on an order (charge, decline, refund, capture). Multi-state lifecycle; ERP-FIN AR sees settled payments via handoff.
GL posting produced by a pay_run, decomposed by cost_center / department / earning_code / deduction_code into debit and credit lines. The payroll-to-finance handoff payload.
Partner Capital Account statement per LP per close period: contributions, distributions, gains/losses, fees, ending balance. Sent to LPs; submit-locked once distributed.
Card-handler security-awareness training record (PCI DSS 12.6).

Calculated workforce KPIs and metrics: time-to-fill, attrition rate, retention rate, span-of-control, internal-mobility rate, training completion rate, cost-per-hire, time-to-productivity. Derived from HCM, ATS, LMS, Payroll event streams. PA is the master of the calculated KPI definitions and the materialized metric values; source systems master the underlying events.
Individual goal or OKR with owner, period, metric, weight, status, alignment to organizational objectives. Reviewed within performance_reviews cycles.
Per-cycle per-worker review artifact: self-assessment, manager assessment, ratings, narrative, calibration outcome. Drives merit_recommendations and succession_plans.

Citizen or business submission requesting a license or permit: applicant, permit type (building / business / professional / event / environmental), submission date, jurisdiction, supporting documents, fees due, status (submitted / under-review / approved / denied / withdrawn). Scope-qualified to avoid collision with ATS, IDP, banking, healthcare applications.

Field inspection tied to a permit (pre-construction, in-progress, final, complaint-driven): inspection type, scheduled date, inspector, location, outcome (pass / fail / conditional), required corrections, follow-up inspection. Scope-qualified vs CLIN-DEV / EAM / FSM inspections.
A buyer or user persona: role, goals, pains, and buying triggers, referenced by messaging and content.
Context-aware branching logic (IF segment X THEN show variant Y) applied to experiences.
Owner / client relationship for veterinary practice: contact info, payment method on file, communication preferences, household-pet-list, financial-balance history.
Per-recipient outcome of a phishing simulation (clicked, reported, ignored).
Configured simulated-phishing campaign for security-awareness training (PCI DSS 12.6).
A business or technical goal a team commits to for a program increment, scored on planned versus actual business value at the inspect-and-adapt review.
Host-pickup-site, depot, or on-farm pickup point with operating hours, member-self-serve capacity.

Definition of a single attribute available to PIM products: data type, validation rules, attribute group, locale-awareness, and channel-specific overrides. Distinct from runtime attribute values on a product instance.

Hierarchical taxonomy node used to classify PIM products. Multiple parallel taxonomies coexist (merchandising tree, channel-specific trees, ERP category tree); each one's tree lives in this table with a parent_category_id self-reference.

Image, video, 3D model, or document asset tied to one or more PIM products. Carries rights metadata, renditions / derivatives, and CDN-delivery URLs. The DAM slice that lives inside PIM in v1; can be split out to a DAM domain when warranted.

The merchandising-master record for a sellable SKU as PIM models it: a hub of attributes, descriptions, variants, categorizations, translations, digital assets, and channel-specific overrides. Distinct from B2C-COMM commerce_products (storefront runtime view) and PLM engineering_parts (engineering record). Authoritative for marketing / catalog content; consumed by commerce, inventory, CPQ, and marketplaces.

Definition of an outbound publishing channel: marketplace seller portals, merchant feeds, storefront platforms, retailer feeds, GDSN datapools, or a custom partner endpoint. Holds destination-schema mapping rules, credentials, and per-channel attribute overrides.
A single publish run of a product (or batch) to a syndication channel. Carries queue position, run status, per-record validation results, and rejection reasons from the destination.
Locale-keyed string variant of an attribute or description on a PIM product or attribute. Drives multi-language publishing; can be machine-generated, human-translated, or a hybrid pipeline.
Specific size / color / locale / pack-size variant of a parent PIM product. Each variant has its own SKU, can have its own publish state, and inherits attribute defaults from the parent.
Execution instance of a data pipeline: runtime status, lineage snapshot, error state. References `data_pipelines` (DATA-AI-PLAT-mastered).
Sales-process taxonomy: stage definitions, exit criteria, default probability, allowed-next-stage transitions. The configuration object behind the opportunity pipeline.
An append-only record of plan approvals, locks, and the downstream push events.
A saved snapshot of the plan at a point in time, for comparison and audit.
Shelf-layout and product-placement compliance vs corporate planogram standards: deviation, remediation, photo evidence, visual compliance verification.
Per-pass planting event: seed variety, rate, depth, date, weather; ISOBUS-compliant.
CI/CD wired into cluster: GitOps, fleet orchestration, in-cluster build and deploy pipelines.

Resolved configurations of a configurable product: a specific combination of option-and-variant selections that the configurator engine has validated against the 150% BOM and configuration rules. Each variant is a sellable / buildable configuration with its own price, lead time, and resolved BOM.
Staff-augmentation or statement-of-work requisition: scope, role, rate range, duration, location, hiring manager, supplier-tier rules. Drives supplier distribution and candidate submission.
Record that a user read, understood, and acknowledged a policy; timestamp, version, medium, completion evidence.
Individual coverage line within an insurance_policy: line of business, coverage code, limit amount, deductible, coinsurance %, effective period. Determines claim eligibility and adjudication.
ESG and diversity metric submission per portfolio company per reporting period. Drives SFDR Article 8/9 disclosures and LP-side ESG reporting.
KPI submission cycle per portfolio company per reporting period (monthly / quarterly). Captures ARR, headcount, runway, cash, gross margin, NPS, churn.
Fair-value mark per portfolio company per close cycle, per ASC 820 methodology. LP-side valuation distinct from issuer-side 409A valuations.
Investee company held by one or more funds. Carries headline financials, board composition, current ownership %, exit status, sector tagging.
A large body of work in the portfolio backlog that is funded, analyzed, and delivered through a kanban funnel before decomposing into features.
A ship-store retail sale of non-fuel goods, paid at the register or posted to a boater house account.

Projected need for specific roles derived from the capacity model: which positions, when, where, at what level. Feeds the requisition pipeline — approved demand becomes an authorized requisition in ATS via the headcount.approved handoff.

FCRA-mandated notice sent to a candidate before a final adverse-action decision based on a consumer report. Carries a copy of the report and Summary of Rights, and opens a waiting period (typically 5 business days) during which the candidate may dispute findings before the final adverse-action notice issues.

ATS-owned pre-employment record covering the post-offer-acceptance window before the new-hire start date: paperwork in flight, background check pending, pre-boarding tasks open. At start-date the pre-employee row is reconciled into HCM-mastered `employees` (the canonical employee record). HCM owns the canonical employee record; ATS owns the pre-employee lifecycle stage so recruiting and HCM can each move at their own pace.

ML / statistical model outputs deployed in PA: flight-risk scores, performance trajectory, internal-mobility likelihood. Carries the model identifier, training window, target metric, and the materialized scores per employee. Consumes employees and employment_events as features.
Proactive forecast emitted before symptoms surface: predicted capacity exhaustion, predicted failure of a CI based on degradation pattern, predicted SLO breach within the burn-rate window.
Gating logic that controls path progression: required completions, scores, certifications, or competencies.
Per-vehicle-class PM schedule template: trigger basis (mileage / engine hours / calendar time / DTC), task list, due-date generation rules.
Calculation engine: tiered/volume discounts, seat-based pricing, duration-based pricing, bundle discounts, segment overrides.

An activity execution within a process instance: a service task, script, call activity, gateway, or event, with its own lifecycle (activated, completed, failed, compensated) and the job dispatched to a task worker.

Resource-constrained or time-trapped steps in a process: high-wait-time activities, resource queue depth, throughput loss points. Carries activity name, severity, estimated throughput impact, recommended mitigation.

Diagnostic from conformance checking: comparison of event log vs reference process model, flagging deviations with severity, deviation_type (missing / extra / out-of-order / timing), trace-level root cause. Supports regulatory audit.

A deployed, executable process model (BPMN or code-defined) with a unique key and version. Instances are started from a definition; a new deployment publishes a new version while running instances stay pinned to the version they started on.

An append-only record of a single state change in the engine (instance started, activity completed, variable updated, incident raised). The immutable execution history used for replay, recovery, and as the source log downstream process mining consumes.

A blocked execution: a job that exhausted its retries, an unhandled error, or a failed condition that halts an activity until an operator resolves it. Carries the failure detail and the activity it is attached to.

A single running (or completed) execution of a process definition, holding the current token position, scope variables, and a correlation key. The durable, recoverable unit the engine advances through activities and gateways.

A single execution of a process simulation scenario (Monte Carlo or discrete-event) against a business_process_model, with inputs (resource pools, cost/time variables), outputs (throughput, bottleneck nodes), and run metadata.
